# Gospel of Philip — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, pp. 51-86 | Coptic

---

## Chapter 1

**1** A Hebrew makes another Hebrew, and such a person is called a proselyte. But a proselyte does not make a proselyte. Some exist as they are and produce others like themselves, while still others simply come into existence.

**2** The slave seeks only freedom but does not seek the estate of his master. The son is not only a son but lays claim to the inheritance of the father.

**3** Those who inherit the dead are themselves dead, and they inherit dead things. Those who inherit the living are themselves alive, and they inherit both the living and the dead.

**4** The dead inherit nothing. For how could a dead person inherit? If one who is dead inherits what is living, that person will not die, but the dead one shall live even more abundantly.

**5** A Gentile does not die, for he has never lived so as to be able to die. One who has believed the truth has lived, and this one risks death — for he is alive.

**6** Since Christ came, the world has been created, cities have been established, and the dead have been carried out for burial.

**7** When we were Hebrews we were orphans, with only a mother. But when we became Christians we acquired both a father and a mother.

**8** Those who sow in winter reap in summer. The winter is the world; the summer is the other aeon. Let us sow in the world that we may harvest in summer. Because of this it is not fitting for us to pray in winter.

**9** What comes forth from winter is summer. But if anyone reaps in winter, he will not actually reap but will uproot, for that season does not produce fruit. [...] Not only [...] comes in this manner [...] but also the Sabbath is barren.

**10** Christ came to ransom some, to save others, to redeem others. He ransomed those who were strangers and made them his own. And he set apart those who were already his — those whom he gave as a pledge according to his will.

**11** It was not only when he appeared that he voluntarily laid down his life, but he voluntarily laid down his life from the very day the world came into being. Then he came first to take it back, since it had been given as a pledge. It fell into the hands of robbers and was taken captive, but he saved it. He redeemed both the good and the evil in the world.

**12** The light and the darkness, life and death, the right and the left are brothers of one another. It is not possible for the good to relinquish the evil, nor for the evil to relinquish the good, nor for life to relinquish death, nor for death to relinquish life. For this reason each one will dissolve into its original nature. But those who are exalted above the world are incapable of dissolution — they are eternal.

**13** The names given to worldly things are profoundly deceptive, for they divert the heart from the real to the unreal. Thus whoever hears the word "God" does not perceive what is real but perceives what is unreal. So also with "the Father" and "the Son" and "the Holy Spirit" and "life" and "light" and "resurrection" and "the Church" — and all the rest. People do not perceive the real but perceive only the unreal, unless they have come to know the real. The names heard in the world are deceptive. If they were in the aeon, they would not be used as names in the world at all times, nor would they be assigned to worldly things. They have their end in the aeon.

**14** There is one name that is not uttered in the world — the name the Father bestowed upon the Son. It is above every other name. This is the Father's own name: the Son would not have become the Father had he not clothed himself in the name of the Father. Those who possess this name know it but do not speak it. Those who do not possess it do not know it.

**15** But truth brought names into being in the world for our sake, because it is not possible to teach truth without names. Truth is one, yet it is also many, and so for our sake she teaches this one thing through the many.

**16** The archons wanted to deceive mankind, since they saw that mankind had a kinship with what is truly good. They took the names of the good and attached them to the not-good, so that through the names they might deceive him and bind him to what is not good. And as a result — what a service they rendered! For they caused people to abandon the free things and take for themselves what is bound.

**17** The farmer cannot practice his trade without [...] water. Likewise, it is impossible to build anything without water and fire [...]. The farmer harvests because of water and earth.

**18** God is a dyer. Just as good dyes — which are called "true" dyes — dissolve together with the things that are dyed in them, so it is with those whom God has dyed. Since his dyes are immortal, they become immortal through his colors. Now God dips those whom he dips in water.

**19** It is not possible for anyone to perceive anything of the things that truly exist unless he becomes like them. It is not so with the person in the world: he sees the sun without becoming the sun, and he sees the heaven and the earth and all other things without becoming them. But in the truth it is otherwise. You saw something of that place, and you became those things. You saw the Spirit — you became spirit. You saw Christ — you became Christ. You saw the Father — you shall become the Father. So in this world you see everything yet do not see yourself. But in that place you see yourself — for you shall become what you see.

**20** Faith receives; love gives. No one will be able to receive without faith. No one will be able to give without love. Because of this, in order that we may truly receive, we believe. And in order that we may truly give — since one who does not give has nothing — we love.

**21** Before Christ came, there was no bread in the world. In paradise — the place where Adam was — there were many trees and food for the animals, but no wheat for man. Man used to feed as the animals do. But when Christ, the perfect man, came, he brought bread from heaven so that mankind might be nourished with human food.

**22** The archons thought it was by their own power and will that they did what they did. But the Holy Spirit was secretly accomplishing everything through them according to its will.

**23** Truth, which existed from the beginning, is sown everywhere. And many see it being sown, but few are those who see it being reaped.

**24** Some say, "Mary was conceived by the Holy Spirit." They are in error. They do not know what they say. When did a woman ever conceive by a woman? Mary is the virgin whom no power defiled. She is a great anathema to the Hebrew apostles and to the apostolic men. This virgin whom no power defiled [...] the powers defile themselves.

**25** And the Lord would not have said, "My Father who is in heaven," unless he had another father. He would simply have said, "My Father."

**26** The Lord said to the disciples [...]: "Go into every house and bring what is yours from there. Bring what belongs to the Father's house, but do not take or remove anything."

**27** "Jesus" is a hidden name; "Christ" is a revealed name. For this reason "Jesus" does not exist in any other language, but his name is always "Jesus" as he is called. "Christ" is also his name in Syriac and in Greek; but in all other languages it is "Messiah." "The Nazarene" is the revealed form of the hidden name.

**28** Baptism is "the holy" and it is the highest; redemption is "the holy of holies"; the bridal chamber is "the holy of holies" — the holiest of all.

**29** Baptism includes resurrection and redemption; the redemption is in the bridal chamber. But the bridal chamber is in that which is superior to [...]. You will not find [...].

**30** Those who pray for Jerusalem love Jerusalem. Jerusalem is the vision of peace. Jerusalem contemplates Jerusalem. The righteous love Jerusalem.

**31** The holy ones of holiness shall be nourished by truth. [...] There were some who [...] the beasts [...].

**32** In this world those who put on garments are superior to the garments. In the kingdom of heaven the garments are superior to those who have put them on.

**33** It is through water and fire that the whole place shall be purified — the visible by the visible, and the hidden by the hidden. There are things hidden through visible things. There is water within water; there is fire within the chrism.

**34** Jesus approached them all by stealth. For he did not reveal himself as he truly was, but he revealed himself in the manner in which they would be able to see him. He appeared to them all: he revealed himself to the great as great, he revealed himself to the small as small, he revealed himself to the angels as an angel and to men as a man. Because of this his Word was hidden from everyone. Some looked at him and supposed they were seeing themselves. But when he appeared to his disciples in glory on the mountain, he was not small. He had become great. But he made the disciples great so that they could see him in his greatness.

**35** He said on that day in the eucharistic prayer: "You who have joined the perfect light with the Holy Spirit, unite us with the angels as well." Do not despise the lamb, for without it it is not possible to see the king.

**36** No one will be able to go before the king if he is naked. The one who comes from heaven will be clothed if he has put on the light.

**37** Water and fire and light and the Holy Spirit are four powers. The perfect man makes use of all of them — for purification and for vivification. The [...] of the bridal chamber [...] by fire and light.

**38** The Holy Spirit breathes through everyone. The powers [...] those beneath their power [...].

**39** The archons do not know where one who has true understanding comes from, for he has no desire for them to know, lest they trouble him. Will he not then disclose himself when he appears to them?

**40** The cup of prayer contains wine and water. It serves as a type of the blood for which thanks is given. And it is filled with the Holy Spirit, and it belongs entirely to the perfect man. When we drink it, we shall receive the perfect man.

**41** The living water is a body. It is right for us to clothe ourselves in the living man. When one comes to go down into the water, he strips himself and says: "I go down so that I may receive."

**42** A horse sires a horse, a man begets a man, a god brings forth a god. The bridegroom and the bride: so it is. [...] No Jew [...] from a Jew comes a Jew. Such also is the Christian lineage.

**43** Those who say they will die first and then rise are in error. If they do not first receive the resurrection while they live, they will receive nothing when they die. So also when speaking of baptism, they say: "Baptism is a great thing, because if one receives it, he will live."

**44** Philip the apostle said: "Joseph the carpenter planted a garden because he needed wood for his craft. It was he who made the cross from the trees he had planted. His own offspring hung on what he had planted. His offspring was Jesus, and the planting was the cross. But the tree of life is in the middle of the garden, and from the olive tree came the chrism, and from the chrism the resurrection."

**45** This world is a corpse-eater. All the things eaten within it are dead as well. Truth is a life-eater. Therefore no one nourished by truth will die. Jesus came from that place and brought food. And to those who wished it, he gave life so that they might not die.

**46** God planted a garden. Man lived in the garden [...] there were not many trees [...] but there was an abundance of trees and neither animal food nor the fruit of [...] what [...] I desired. But I [...] what they wished [...] This was the garden of God [...] and it gives life.

**47** I ate from [...] that place [...] a man of God [...] killed animals [...]. He prepared animal food there. But when he prepared animal food [...] he satisfied the animals [...] but he threw the men into poverty. [...] God [...] man [...].

**48** It was the will of God that man should eat and the animals should not eat. When Adam ate, the animals also ate. Eating the fruit of the tree — which was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil — they brought death upon themselves and the animals.

**49** The Eucharist is Jesus, for he is called in Hebrew "Pharisath," which means "the one who is spread out," for Jesus came to crucify the world.

**50** The Lord went into the dye works of Levi. He took seventy-two colors and threw them into the vat. He brought them all out white. And he said: "Even so has the Son of Man come as a dyer."

**51** The Wisdom who is called "barren" is the mother of the angels. And the companion of the Savior is Mary Magdalene. [...] loved her more than all the disciples, and used to kiss her often on the [...]. The rest of the disciples [...] expressed disapproval. They said to him: "Why do you love her more than all of us?" The Savior answered and said to them: "Why do I not love you as I love her? When a blind man and one who sees stand together in darkness, they are no different from one another. When the light comes, then he who sees will see the light, and he who is blind will remain in the darkness."

**52** The Lord said: "Blessed is the one who is before he came into being. For whoever is, was, and shall be."

**53** The superiority of mankind is not visible but lies in what is hidden. Consequently he has dominion over the animals who are stronger than him in visible and hidden terms. This gives him his survival. But if man separates from them, they kill and bite and devour him.

**54** No great thing can come into being if the small does not first exist. Nor can what is holy exist if the visible does not first exist. For indeed, the hidden would be dissolved were it not for the visible and the hidden together.

**55** There is water within water, there is fire within fire, there is light within light. This is the baptism of truth.

**56** The Lord did everything in a mystery: a baptism and a chrism and a Eucharist and a redemption and a bridal chamber.

**57** He said: "I came to make the things below like the things above, and the things outside like the things inside. I came to unite them in that place." [...] He is revealed through types and images.

**58** Those who say, "There is a heavenly man and there is one who is above him," are mistaken. For it is this heavenly man who is called "the one below," and it is he to whom the hidden belongs who is above him. It is right to say "the inner and the outer," and "what is outside the outer." Because of this the Lord called destruction the "outer darkness" — there is nothing beyond it.

**59** He said: "My Father who is in secret — go into your inner chamber and close the door behind you and pray to your Father who is in secret." The one who is within everything is the fullness. There is nothing more inward than he. This is what they call "the uppermost."

**60** Before Christ, some came from a place they would no longer enter, and went to a place they would no longer leave. But Christ came. Those who had gone in he brought out, and those who had gone out he brought back in.

**61** When Eve was still within Adam, death did not exist. When she was separated from him, death came into being. If she enters into him again and he receives her to himself, death will be no more.

**62** "My God, my God, why, O Lord, have you forsaken me?" He spoke these words on the cross. For he had separated from that place.

**63** The Lord rose from the dead. He became as he was before, but now his body was perfect flesh. Now our flesh is imperfect. But this is his flesh, which is [...] the true flesh.

**64** Truth did not come into the world naked, but it came in types and images. The world will not receive it in any other way. There is a rebirth and there is an image of rebirth. It is necessary to be reborn through the image. What is the resurrection and the image? It is necessary that it arise through the image. The bridal chamber and the image — it is through the image that one must enter into the truth: this is the restoration.

**65** For those who have received it, it is necessary not only to receive the resurrection but also the Holy Spirit. The Father and the Son are simple names; the Holy Spirit is a double name. For they are everywhere — above and below, in the hidden and in the manifest. The Holy Spirit is manifest below, and in the hidden above.

**66** In those who are holy, the Holy Spirit is holy. The evil spirit breathes below, in the hidden realm. And those who are wise and good and holy seek their strength from above. And though they are seen, they are not troubled. They are not seduced by either the lower or the higher powers when they choose to be free.

**67** The fear in a person does not fear a beast that is greater than himself; to the beast that is larger he attributes intelligence or beauty or [...].

**68** The slave seeks only his freedom; he does not seek the wealth of his master. But the son, who is the true heir, not only possesses the right to the patrimony of the father but claims it for himself.

**69** Those who inherit the dead are themselves dead and they inherit dead things. Those who inherit the living are themselves alive and they inherit both the living and the dead.

**70** The dead inherit nothing. For how shall a dead man inherit? When the dead man inherits the living, he will not die but will on the contrary live all the more.

**71** A pagan does not die, for he has never lived in order to die. One who has believed in the truth has lived, and this one is in danger of dying — for he is alive.

**72** Since Christ came, the world has been made, cities have been founded, and the dead have been carried out.

**73** When I was a child, I was nurtured among the great. [...] It is beneficial to be nurtured among the great. [...] As for what belongs to the Father — the child will not receive the inheritance if he is a minor. The master of the estate would not give it to him before he comes of age.

**74** In the same way, the son must not only be a son but must himself become the father.

**75** Those who receive the chrism are called "anointed ones." The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit — it is not fitting to call the Father "Christ," nor the Son "Christ," nor the Holy Spirit "Christ." None of these has the name as their own. The name is given only to the one who has been anointed — and this by the Father.

**76** [...] The Father's name is the Son. He did not keep it hidden; it existed. The Son himself had no name before the Father gave it to him. His name, when revealed, is the Father himself.

**77** The Word of the Lord said to the disciples: "Eat my flesh and drink my blood." Whoever says this, overturns the world. The flesh is the Word, and the blood is the Holy Spirit. Whoever has received these has food and drink and clothing.

**78** I find fault with those who say that the flesh will not rise. Then they are wrong in both respects. You say the flesh will not rise — then tell me what will rise, that we may honor you. You say the spirit in the flesh, and also the light in the flesh. But this word too is flesh. The Word became flesh: it was through this flesh that the Word rose — and everything was united through the flesh and the Word.

**79** This resurrection does not concern the naked soul. What then shall rise? It is the flesh together with the soul together with the spirit.

**80** The soul and spirit came into being from water and fire and light — the child of the bridal chamber — from water and fire and light.

**81** Fire is the chrism; light is the fire. I do not speak of the fire that has no form, but of the other fire, whose form is white and which is beautiful luminous light, and which bestows beauty.

**82** Truth does not come into the world naked but in types and images. It cannot be received in any other way. There is a resurrection and there is an image of the resurrection. One must truly be reborn through the image. What is the resurrection? The image must arise through the image. The bridal chamber and the image: through the image one must enter into the truth — this is the restoration.

**83** It is right for those who have received [...] not only to receive redemption but to enter within. [...] Those who receive are united through the Word and they receive [...].

**84** Is it not right to pray during both night and day? And one who receives the light [...] does not pray by day — he himself is light. The man who has received the Word [...] does not receive it as a gift. He [...].

**85** If you are [...] before the days and say [...], all those who believe in him [...].

**86** The light is a model for those in this world. It was not great at first. But when it increased to perfection it became great. And it gave to the world and to the aeon alike.

**87** Those who are clothed in the perfect light — the powers and the angels cannot discern their nakedness and are unable to detain them. But one will put on this light in the mystery, in the union of the bridal chamber.

**88** If the woman had not separated from the man, she would not have died together with the man. His separation became the beginning of death. Because of this Christ came to rectify the separation which had existed from the beginning and to reunite the two; and to those who had died in the separation he would give life and unite them.

**89** But the woman is united with her husband in the bridal chamber. Indeed those who have been united in the bridal chamber will no longer be separated from one another. Because of this Eve separated from Adam: because she had not been united with him in the bridal chamber.

**90** The soul of Adam came into being through a breath. His partner was given to him from the Spirit, who is [...] his mother. His soul was given to him. [...] But the soul that was given to him — it is this which [...].

**91** The Word produced the things it desired. All that it produced, it produced in secret. But the bridal chamber produces openly. Nothing is hidden on the day of the bridal chamber. None of those who share in the celebration of the bridegroom are hidden.

**92** Abraham [...] circumcised, in order to teach us that it is fitting to destroy the flesh of the world.

**93** As long as the intestines of a person are concealed, the person is alive and well. If the intestines are exposed and come out, the person will die. So also, as long as the root of evil is hidden it is strong. But when it is recognized it is destroyed, and when it is exposed it perishes. For this reason the Word says: "Already the axe is laid at the root of the trees."

**94** It will not merely cut — what is cut will sprout again. But the axe digs until it brings up the root. Jesus pulled up the root of the whole realm, while others had done so only partially. As for us — let each one of us dig up the root of evil that is within him and pull it out from his heart. It will be uprooted when we recognize it.

**95** But if we are ignorant of it, it takes root within us and produces its fruit in our hearts. It rules over us; we are its slaves. It takes us captive so that we do what we do not want, and what we want we do not do. It is powerful because we have not recognized it. As long as it exists it is active.

**96** Ignorance is the mother of all evils. Ignorance will result in death. Those who come from ignorance neither existed nor exist nor will exist. [...] When truth comes, all these things will be perfected.

**97** When truth comes, the perfect things will be revealed, the hidden things made manifest, and the holy things declared. Truth will reveal what is hidden. It will call the elect by name, and the Father will cause them to inherit what is prepared for them.

**98** Those who have it — from them it will be taken; those who do not have it — even what they have will be taken. This is the justice of the world.

**99** The Master of the universe is not merely a lord but is the Father — for a "master" has no son, but a father does have a son. We call him "master" because we have not yet come to know him.

**100** The Word said: "Ask and you shall receive, seek and you shall find, knock and it shall be opened to you." Let us ask in order that we may receive; let us knock at the gate of the treasury of the wedding feast.

**101** If we pray for the Holy Spirit in the night and in the day, we give thanks [...].

**102** The Son of Man came from above. He said [...]. He humbled himself to the point of death. When he had died and risen, those who [...] knew him. So it was possible for the perfect to be revealed in the darkness.

**103** The holy man is entirely holy, including his body. For if he has received bread, he sanctifies it; or the cup, or anything else that he receives — he purifies them as well.

**104** And how will he not also purify his body?

**105** As Jesus perfected the water of baptism, so he expelled death. Because of this we go down into the water, but we do not go down into death, lest we be poured out into the spirit of the world.

**106** When that wind blows, it brings the winter. When the Holy Spirit breathes, the summer comes.

**107** Whoever knows the truth is free, and the free man does not sin, for "the one who sins is the slave of sin." Truth is the mother; knowledge is the father. Those who are considered by the world to be unable to sin are called "free" by the world. The knowledge of the truth merely lifts up their hearts — that is, it makes them consider themselves free without making them truly conscious of their own hearts.

**108** Love builds up. Whoever has been set free through knowledge is a slave on account of love for those who have not yet attained the freedom of knowledge. Knowledge equips them to become free.

**109** Love never calls anything its own, yet [...] everything is of love. It does not say "this is mine" or "that is mine" — but "all these are yours."

**110** Spiritual love is wine and fragrance. All those who anoint themselves with it take pleasure in it. While those who are anointed stand by, those who stand nearby also enjoy the fragrance. If those who are anointed leave and depart, those who are nearby but not anointed remain in their unpleasant smell. The Samaritan gave nothing to the wounded man except wine and oil — that is, nothing but the chrism. And it healed his wounds.

**111** "Love covers a multitude of sins." Love covers no sin. Love renders many sins invisible.

**112** The light that was joined to the darkness did not emerge from the darkness. But now it shines within the darkness and in the light. The perfect light will shine in every place. When it is perfect, it comes to birth.

**113** If you say "I am a Jew," no one is moved. If you say "I am a Roman," no one is disturbed. If you say "I am a Greek, a barbarian, a slave, or free," no one is troubled. But if you say "I am a Christian" — the [...] will tremble. Would that I might receive [...] this name which [...].

**114** God is a man-eater. Because of this, mankind is sacrificed to him. Before mankind was sacrificed, animals were being sacrificed. For those to whom they were sacrificed were not gods.

**115** Glass vessels and earthen vessels are both made by fire. But if glass vessels break they are made again, for they came into being through breath. But if earthen vessels break they are destroyed, for they came into being without breath.

**116** An ass which turns a millstone walked a hundred miles. When it was set loose, it found itself in the same place. Some men make many journeys but have no destination. When evening came upon them they saw neither city nor village, neither created thing nor nature, neither power nor angel. In vain did those wretched ones labor.

**117** The Eucharist is Jesus. For in Hebrew he is called Pharisath, meaning "the one who is extended," because Jesus came to crucify the world.

**118** The Lord went into the dye works of Levi. He took seventy-two colors and threw them into the vat. He brought them all out white. And he said: "Even so has the Son of Man come as a dyer."

**119** The Wisdom who is called "barren" is the mother of the angels. And the companion of the Savior is Mary Magdalene. The Savior loved her more than all the disciples, and he used to kiss her often on her [...]. The rest of the disciples were offended by this and expressed disapproval. They said to him: "Why do you love her more than all of us?" The Savior answered and said to them: "Why do I not love you as I love her? When a blind man and one who sees stand together in darkness, they are no different from one another. When the light comes, then the one who sees will see the light, and the one who is blind will remain in the darkness."

**120** The Lord said: "Blessed is the one who exists before he came into being. For whoever is, was, and shall be."

**121** The superiority of mankind is not visible but lies in what is hidden. Therefore he masters the animals who are stronger than he in both visible and hidden respects. This gives him his survival. But when man separates from them, they slay, bite, and devour him.

**122** The one who has come to possess the knowledge of truth is free. The free man does not sin. "The one who sins is the slave of sin." Truth is the mother; knowledge is the father.

**123** Those who are prevented from sinning — the world calls them "free." The knowledge of truth only lifts up their hearts, which is to say it makes them arrogant. But this is also a form of freedom.

**124** The bridal chamber is not for the animals, nor for the slaves, nor for defiled women — but for free men and virgins.

**125** Through the Holy Spirit we are born again, and we are born through Christ in a twofold manner. We are anointed through the Spirit. When we were born, we were united.

**126** None shall be able to see the bridal chamber without becoming a son of the bridal chamber. A Nazarene — that is, "the one who reveals hidden things." It is not possible for the son not to be born, and it is not possible for the [...] not to come.

**127** The holy man is entirely holy, down to his very body. For if he has received the bread, he sanctifies it; or the cup, or anything else that he receives — he purifies these as well. And how shall he not also purify the body?

---

**Translator's Notes (LOGOS):**
- The five sacraments (baptism, chrism, eucharist, redemption, bridal chamber) are treated as progressively more interior rites, with the bridal chamber as the culmination. This text reflects Valentinian sacramental theology in which outer rites correspond to inner spiritual realities.
- The repeated motif of hiddenness (types, images, concealment) reflects Valentinian Platonism: the material world is a shadow of higher realities; truth is always mediated.
- The Mary Magdalene passage (vv. 51, 119) contains a manuscript lacuna before the body part kissed; the text does not specify "on the mouth" — only "on the [...]." Responsible translation preserves this gap rather than speculating.
- "Bridal chamber" (nymphon) is consistently preserved as a technical term. The Greek *nymphon* denotes not a bridal bed but the chamber itself — the place of union and mystery.
- The text employs a recurring duality structure (light/dark, visible/hidden, inner/outer) that serves its theological argument: salvation is the reunion of separated pairs.

---
